content:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in model load failures in us-east-1. Autoscaler reports multiple node flaps and several pods failing at model deserialization. Paging oncall.

kai: Got the page, looking now.

pete: I’m awake. can you paste the logs?

kai: attaching tail of failing pod logs ->
```
2026-03-15T02:14:03Z ERROR model_loader: deserialization failed for artifact=redwood-7b.q4f size=2.1GB error="python msgpack.UnpackValueError: unpack(b)"
2026-03-15T02:14:03Z WARN runtime: falling back to disk streaming
2026-03-15T02:14:05Z FATAL cuda: cuInit() failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT
2026-03-15T02:14:05Z ERROR container: oom-kill (oom_score_adj=-1000) pid=4321 process=llm-server
```

maria: seeing same across 3 nodes in the group, CPU okay but memory spike on attachment. Metrics: Model load success rate dropped to 40% for the last 10m; 503s up.

ops-bot: Incident severity -> P1 (automated rule: >30% model load failure + node flaps). Incident created.

kai: quick remediation options: 1) disable preload/warmup for the model, 2) pin to smaller variant (redwood-7b-compact), 3) cordon/drain affected nodes and reprovision, 4) fallback routing to dedicated pool in us-west. Suggest we do 1 and 4 immediately.

pete: +1 to disable warmup and route traffic to us-west. Can we toggle routing at the edge?

maria: yes, can push a routing policy changelist:
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","condition":"region==us-east-1 && model==redwood-7b","action":"route->us-west-1-pool","ttl":600}
```

sara: starting the edge routing change now, will post when done.

kai: I'm SSHing into one of the failing nodes to check dmesg and docker logs. If this is OOM-at-load, we may need to change the container's mem limit temporarily.

maria: Customer impact: two enterprise customers showing 100% model load errors on some endpoints, small PLG customers see elevated latency and 5xxs. CS notified.

pete: Assigning incident commander to me. @sara you coordinate routing. @kai investigate node state and see if serialization code has changed in last deploy. @maria handle customer comms with status.

sara: routing change applied: edge rule active, traffic to redwood-7b in us-east now 85% routed to us-west. Monitoring for error rate drop.

ops-bot: Edge routing change: success. Propagation 20s.

kai: dmesg from node-7: 
```
[ 6221.342] Out of memory: Killed process 4321 (llm-server) total-vm:2432100kB, anon-rss:2200000kB
[ 6221.342] oom_reaper: reaped process 4321
```
Container memory limit was 4Gi, model requires ~5.5Gi to deserialize into quantized tensors on GPU.

maria: any recent artifact changes? We had an automated packaging tweak yesterday that touched msgpack usage.

kai: git blame points to artifact-builder change: commit bf3a2c5 changed how weights are serialized -> switched to msgpack with custom hooks. Might be incompatible with older runtime.

pete: Possible root: combination of serialization format change + memory threshold assumption -> deserialization into memory triggers OOM then CUDA init fails.

sara: CS on call updated customers: "We're mitigating by routing traffic away from affected nodes and working on restore. Expect degraded service for some models in us-east; no model outputs lost at rest."

maria: temporary mitigations executed: 1) routing 85% to us-west, 2) increased pod mem limit to 8Gi for new loads in a test pool, 3) disabled warmup in us-east for redwood-7b. Monitoring.

kai: repro steps I ran in staging: pull artifact from S3, run deserialization with current runtime -> crash at msgpack.UnpackValueError unless we use builder commit bf3a2c5's loader. So mismatch between build-time serialization and runtime loader.

pete: action items:
- rollback artifact-builder change in next deploy (maria)
- add compatibility check in model registry (kai)
- add guard in runtime to stream-deserialize instead of eager allocation when size > threshold (eng-runtime backlog item)
- write customer postmortem and timeline (sara)

sara: I'm taking 04:00 -> 08:00 handoff. @maria you'll be my primary for comms if I need help.

kai: added temporary guard in runtime: if deserialized_size > container_mem_limit * 0.8 -> switch to stream mode. Pushed as hotfix to canary.

ops-bot: Deploy canary hotfix to canary-pool -> success.

maria: error rates down to 7% for redwood-7b after routing + hotfix. Two enterprise customers still impacted; they routed to us-west and reported partial recovery.

pete: preparing incident timeline and impact notes. Key root cause: serialization format change in artifact-builder created incompat with runtime eager-deserialize path, causing OOM on model load leading to container termination and CUDA init failures on restart; exacerbated by node flaps in the autoscaler.

sara: handing off incident to morning oncall @maria at 08:00. I'll remain shadow for comms.

maria: will continue monitoring, coordinate rollback of artifact-builder, and start drafting postmortem. I'll escalate to Eng lead for runtime backlog.

pete: thanks all. keeping P1 until rollback validated and affected customers confirm recovery.

oncall-bot: Handoff logged: previous_oncall=kai, new_oncall=maria, handoff_time=4319872800

maria: final note for now — recommend adding a preflight that attempts to instantiate a tiny dummy tensor with the artifact to validate mem footprint before promoting artifact to production.

pete: agreed. adding to postmortem recommendations.
